programme.title: Arena
programme.sub-title: Arena: Harold Pinter - Part One: The Room
programme.desc: Part one of two. A 2002 profile of the acclaimed playwright, exploring the inspiration for his work and visiting the rooms where he wrote in an attempt to identify links between the atmosphere there and the content of his plays. Beginning in Pinter's west London study, the film observes his previous places of work, including the terraced house where he grew up, a theatre dressing room and an apartment lounge. Including scenes from the Almeida Theatre's 2001 production of Pinter's first play The Room, which starred Lindsay Duncan and Keith Allen

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: The concluding part of the profile chronicles how the playwright's critical acclaim launched him to stardom. The film reveals the relationship between his public and private lives, assesses the evolution of his writing style and examines his work in film and television. Plus, a chance to see the TV premiere of Celebration, a tale directed by Pinter which sees a group of friends celebrate in a restaurant over the course of an evening. Lindsay Duncan and Andy de la Tour star. With contributions from Antonia Fraser, Henry Woolf, Kenneth Cranham, Peter Hall and John Pilger

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth plans a nautical supper aboard a borrowed cruiser, but the event does not go to plan. Suburban sitcom, starring Patricia Routledge, Clive Swift and Geoffrey Hughes

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: First episode of the comedy. The death of her husband leaves upper-class snob Audrey fforbes-Hamilton a widow in drastically reduced circumstances, with her beloved ancestral pile up for auction. Starring Penelope Keith and Peter Bowles

programme.title: Life on Earth

programme.title: Eisteddfod 2026 with Huw Stephens
programme.desc: Celebrating the 850th anniversary of Wales's first recorded cultural festival, the National Eisteddfod returns to its historic roots in west Wales, taking place in Llantwd, north Pembrokeshire. Huw bring viewers the musical highlights and stories from across the Maes, from brass bands and polished pop to classical and contemporary music. The festival opens with a landmark performance on the rock and pop stage by Super Furry Animals, making their first Eisteddfod appearance in 30 years, while Huw also explores an exciting mix of contemporary folk, bluegrass, jazz and country at T? Gwerin, including a special 50th-anniversary concert by Welsh folk legends Ar Log

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Petroc Trelawny presents from the Royal Albert Hall as Thomas Adès conducts the National Youth Orchestra on a musical journey to the underworld and back. The programme opens with Liszt's Mephisto Waltz No 1, a whirlwind score based on Nikolaus Lenau's epic poem Faust, followed by Adès' own Dante - Part 2: Purgatorio, the central act of his Grammy Award-winning ballet. To round off the concert, the orchestra delivers the dazzling Symphonie fantastique by Berlioz. Liszt: Mephisto Waltz No 1. Thomas Adès: Dante - Part 2: Purgatorio. Berlioz Symphonie fantastique. National Youth Orchestra, Thomas Adès (conductor)

programme.title: The Brontës Lived Here: Writers' Houses
programme.desc: Margaret Drabble visits Haworth Parsonage and the Yorkshire Moors, home of famous literary family the Brontës and the setting for Emily's Wuthering Heights, investigating how much the sisters' environment affected their work. First broadcast in 1973

programme.title: Lady Antonia Fraser Remembers - The Birthday Party
programme.desc: It was at a 1975 production of his play The Birthday Party that Harold Pinter first met Antonia Fraser, and changed both their lives with the single phrase 'Must you go?'. What followed was a scandal that gripped London's high society, and a marriage that lasted 28 years, until Pinter's death in 2008. in this programme, explains how that original encounter has always meant that the play holds a special meaning for her, despite its unsettling nature, and she looks back fondly on the BBC's 1987 acclaimed adaptation of The Birthday Party, and her husband's performance as mysteriously menacing Goldberg

programme.title: The Birthday Party
programme.desc: It is Stanley's birthday, but the party that is thrown for him is not quite what he was expecting. A 1987 adaptation of Harold Pinter's play, starring Joan Plowright, Robert Lang, Colin Blakely, Kenneth Cranham, Julie Walters and the playwright himself

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Comedy actors Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer travel to the picturesque River Usk in south Wales, where Paul's father first taught him to fish as a young child. The duo discuss their respective childhoods and reflect on their own family lives and values. In their cosy cottage accommodation in the heart of the countryside they compare school photographs and Paul serenades Bob with his guitar. Once outside in the picturesque environment, their quarry is the wild brown trout

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer brave the wild lakes of Essex in search of the mighty carp. They have the latest high-tech equipment to catch the biggest fish they can - and are fully prepared to stay all night if they have to. The pair discuss the true meaning of a mid-life crisis and decide to visit a beauty clinic to see whether there are any suitable treatments available to re-capture their youth. Bob reveals his secret recipe to make the perfect scrambled eggs - but it's not the only thing that shocks Paul

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob Mortimer has harboured a childhood dream to catch a salmon, so together with friend Paul Whitehouse, he sets off for the River Tay in Scotland full of hope and excitement. A ghillie guides them up the intimidating river in a boat and they fish using various methods to catch the elusive fish. They stay in the heart of the Highlands, where Bob cooks Paul a traditional Scottish breakfast and enjoy a swift round of golf before resuming their fishing. The duo also reflect on luck and fate and the part it has played in their lives and later assess whether the trip has lived up to their expectations

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers' Chicken and Egg
programme.sub-title: The Hairy Bikers' Chicken and Egg - UK
programme.desc: The duo set out on a new culinary mission, biking across Europe, the Middle East and America to find and cook the most delicious chicken and egg recipes in the world. They start out on home turf, where they demonstrate how to ensure the perfect roast chicken every time, find out how chickens first came to the UK and make cakes and Welsh rarebit at a country show in Wales. As they celebrate the British passion for poultry, other recipes include chicken and leek suet pudding and scotch eggs

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers' Chicken and Egg

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing

programme.title: The Life of Mammals
programme.desc: David Attenborough examines the hunting tactics of the world's carnivores. Arctic foxes in the frozen north must collect food during warmer times to survive the winter, while the big cats of the southern hemisphere rely on stealth and surprise to catch each meal. The presenter also reveals how leopards and tigers are solitary hunters, coming together only to mate, whereas lions stay in family groups so they can tackle larger prey and better protect their young

programme.title: The Life of Mammals
programme.desc: David Attenborough presents an insight into the most successful animals on the planet. programme.title: The Life of Mammals

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: David Attenborough highlights the curiosities that have led to accusations of forgery, but have ultimately helped assist the rethinking of evolution. programme.title: Rise of the Nazis
programme.sub-title: The First Six Months in Power
programme.desc: It is 1933 and Adolf Hitler is the chancellor of Germany, but he does not have absolute power as there is still a democratic parliament, a head of state and the rule of law. Hitler calls a general election to increase Nazi representation, but a fire in the Reichstag building is blamed on communists - prompting thousands of arrests of left-wingers. Hitler then calls on President von Hindenburg to act and a decree is passed giving the Nazis emergency powers to ban free speech and the right to protest

programme.desc: David Attenborough uses advanced surveillance technology to observe the feeding habits of herbivores, including elephants forced to undertake epic migrations to ensure a steady diet of the plants they need to survive. He also considers the habits of the sloth, which takes a month to digest each meal, and reveals scientific research suggesting that grazing wildebeest do not follow the rains as originally thought, but detect trails of phosphorus in the grass

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programme.desc: David Attenborough highlights the curiosities that have led to accusations of forgery, but have ultimately helped assist the rethinking of evolution. When early explorers brought the first specimen of a duck-billed platypus to England in 1799, it was considered so bizarre it was deemed a hoax. Similarly, the midwife toad became the centre of a scientific storm in the 1920s that led to accusations of fakery

programme.title: Rise of the Nazis
programme.desc: The final episode examines the infamous Night of the Long Knives in late June and early July of 1934, when Adolf Hitler - urged on by Hermann Goering and Heinrich Himmler - ordered a series of political executions on those seen as a threat to the Nazi regime. The most well-known of these was Ernst Roehm, commander and co-founder of the Sturmabteilung, the Nazi Party's militia, whom Hitler had come to see as a potential rival. At least 85 people died during the purge, although the final death toll may have been in the hundreds

programme.title: The Masked Singer

programme.title: Friends

programme.title: Friends
programme.sub-title: The One with the Holiday Armadillo
programme.desc: Phoebe plans to return to her flat and tries desperately to persuade Rachel to join her, while Monica is infuriated by Chandler's inability to tip appropriately. Ross looks after Ben during the holiday season, and dresses as an armadillo to keep him entertained

programme.title: In for a Penny
programme.desc: Stephen Mulhern heads to Barry in the Vale of Glamorgan for the game show in which he travels around the UK setting members of the public unusual challenges, giving them the chance to win anything from the price of their petrol to £1,000 in the final game.

programme.title: How to Lose Weight Well
programme.sub-title: From the Hallelujah to the Weigh Down Diet
programme.desc: Xand van Tulleken and Helen Lawal oversee proceedings as three more pairs road test some of the most popular and talked about diets. Drag queens Jordan and Thomas have one week to drop a dress size ahead of their next performance, best friends Earl and Vince go on six-week faith-based diets to slim down before a forthcoming church celebration, and mums Maria and Jules want to lose weight for a kayaking trip in three months. Xand also investigates whether infrared can make people lighter and if it is possible to offset snacks by exercising at work

programme.title: My Hoarder Mum and Me
programme.desc: A Place in the Sun presenter Jasmine Harman embarks on a personal journey to help her mother Vasoulla overcome her extreme hoarding habit. Over the course of 30 years, the family's five-bedroom London home has become filled from floor to ceiling with clutter, forcing Jasmine's 12-year-old brother Cameron to move out. Debate still rages over whether hoarding should be classified as a mental illness, and Jasmine meets the families of other sufferers to learn how they deal with the problem. Narrated by Rupert Houseman

programme.title: Celebrity Catchphrase
programme.desc: Stephen Mulhern hosts another charity edition of the game show, with Mel Blatt, Michelle Visage and Seann Walsh trying to say what they see as they guess well-known phrases for the chance to win a £50,000 jackpot for their chosen good causes

programme.title: Posh Pawn
programme.desc: More customers arrive at Prestige Pawnbrokers, including a woman and her son, who are hoping to secure a loan against a 71-carat tanzanite ring they bought from a home-shopping channel. Prestige boss James Constantinou takes a shine to a bespoke show motorbike, and must fight against his instinct to claim the vehicle for himself as he seeks a buyer. Plus, a collection of 500 handbags arrives for valuation

First up is a cash builder of up to five questions, after which they have the option of playing between two, three, four or all of the Chasers for increasing amounts of money - and those brave enough to take on all five could walk away with a huge cash prize
